etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin intrudere, from in- + trudere (“to thrust”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To thrust oneself in; to come or enter without invitation, permission, or welcome; to encroach; to trespass.

quote.citation: 1725, Isaac Watts, Logick: Or, The Right Use of Reason in the Enquiry after Truth, […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  John Clark and Richard Hett, […], Emanuel Matthews, […], and Richard Ford, […], published 1726, →OCLC:
quote.text: Some thoughts rise and intrude upon us, while we shun them; others fly from us, when we would hold them.
